title: Pricing/Packaging Back-of-the-Envelope Notes (token math & unit economics)
content:
Context / goals:
- Quick scratchpad to capture unit economics + simple tier ideas for hosted API and Dedicated.
- Focus: token-level cost math, impact of batching & KV caching, simple markup heuristics, and a few starter tier names.
- Don’t overfit numbers to current infra; these are order-of-magnitude estimates we can refine.

Assumptions (back-of-envelope numbers):
- GPU instance baseline: A100-equivalent serving node cost (fully loaded, infra+ops+power): ~$2.00/hr (this is blended across cloud/reserved).
- Throughput (generation): depends on model and batch. Example: 13B FP16-ish -> ~80–150 tok/sec with batching; with quantized kernels maybe 200 tok/sec peak. Use conservative 100 tok/sec per GPU for mixed workload.
- Effective concurrency: with batching and multi-tenant packing we can get ~6 concurrent streams per GPU average.
- Token compute = tokens/sec * hrs -> 100 tok/sec * 3600 = 360k tok/hr. Cost per token compute-only = $2 / 360k = $5.6e-6 per token (~$0.0056 per 1k tokens).
- Add infra overhead (control plane, storage, network, monitoring, egress): assume 2x compute cost => total raw cost per 1k tokens ~= $0.011.
- Embeddings: compute cost per vector depends on model size; typical cheaper model might be ~1/4 the generation cost per vector; ballpark embedding cost per 1k vectors ~= $0.002-0.005.
- Storage/retention for cache/prefix: modest, add as separate line item for heavy caching customers.

Effects of batching & caching (important levers):
- Batching: increases throughput (tokens/sec per GPU) and reduces per-token compute. If we can 2x throughput via batching, cost per 1k tokens halves. But latency-sensitive customers won’t get full benefit.
- KV caching/prefix reuse for chat bots: if 40% of tokens are prefix re-used from KV cache, effective billable tokens drop and cost falls.
- Quantization: INT8/4 reduces kernel cost and memory, enabling higher packing and lower cost by ~30-50% depending on model.

Simple pricing heuristics (hosted API):
- Developer (free tier): 100k tokens/month free; designed for quick testing.
- Starter: $10/month -> 1M tokens included ($0.01 per 1k tokens effective). Good for small prototypes.
- Team: $99/month -> 10M tokens included ($0.0099 per 1k), plus volume discount beyond that.
- Scale / Production (pay-as-you-go): $0.015 per 1k tokens for generation high-quality models; cheaper for quantized variants or smaller models (e.g., $0.007 per 1k on 3B quantized).
- Embeddings: $0.006 per 1k vectors for high-quality embedding model; $0.002 for cheaper embedding variant.
- Rationale: markup applied to raw cost (~2-3x on average) to cover R&D, sales, SRE, and to allow discounts for Dedicated/committed customers. For self-serve SMBs, aim to keep sticker <= $0.01-0.02 per 1k to be attractive.

Dedicated pricing sketch (reserved capacity):
- Offer monthly committed GPU pools with SLOs. Pricing levers: committed hours, reserved throughput gates, support level.
- Example SKU: 1 dedicated GPU-equivalent pool (1k tok/sec sustained) = $X/month. Need mapping from tokens/sec to GPUs: if 1 GPU ~= 100 tok/sec (conservative) then 1k tok/sec ~= 10 gpus.
- If 1 GPU full-cost is $2/hr -> monthly cost per GPU ~ $2 * 24 * 30 = $1440. For 10 GPUs -> $14,400 raw infra. Add margin/ops -> list at $20-30k/month for that pool.
- Offer commit discounts (30-50%) vs hosted pay-as-you-go depending on tenure and SLAs. Also include burst credits and canary/rollout support.

Unit economics examples (toy, to sanity-check):
- Hosted generation: assume average customer uses 1M tokens/month on 13B. Raw cost at $0.011 per 1k = $11. Charge $0.015 per 1k -> revenue = $15. Margin contribution ~$4 per 1M tokens (36% gross margin).
- If customer is latency-sensitive and we need lower batching, raw cost goes up 2-3x -> margin negative unless charged higher. Important to surface 'latency SLO' premium.

Pricing levers and value-based charges:
- Latency SLO premium (e.g., 1.5-3x price for <100ms P50 requirement).
- Model quality premium (larger models cost more). Expose model families with clear per-1k pricing.
- Storage & retention for context/history (charge per GB-month).
- Dedicated/reserved capacity (flat monthly + usage overage).
- Support & Enterprise (SLA, audit logs, compliance): tiered addons.

Tier name ideas (quick):
- Sandbox (free), Developer ($), Team ($$), Business ($$$), Enterprise (custom).
- Or: Play (free), Build, Scale, Mission.

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Need to validate per-GPU throughput numbers across typical model families (3B / 7B / 13B / 70B) and quantization modes. Put together microbench harness results (ask Serving Runtime).
- Better breakdown for infra overheads (network, control plane, storage) — currently guessed as 2x compute. Ops to verify.
- Embedding cost calibration: run 1M vector job through recommended embedding model and measure tokens/sec equivalent.
- Pricing experiments: A/B test per-1k pricing vs included-bucket model to see onramp conversion.

Notes to self:
- Add a simple spreadsheet mapping: model -> tok/sec -> $/1k raw -> suggested public price -> gross margin.
- Get Samir/Maya to sanity-check Dedicated list prices.
- Keep a clear note about latency premium — customers care a lot and economics change dramatically.

Rough action items:
- [ ] Request microbench results from serving-runtime (3B/7B/13B/70B, FP16/INT8).
- [ ] Build quick sheet with model->throughput->cost.
- [ ] Draft initial public pricing page with Developer/Team/Scale tiers.
- [ ] Plan 2 pricing experiments for Q2 2026.

End of scratchpad.

(Informal — do not copy to marketing without cleaning. — Riley)
